title: Finite simplex filtration of a normal-crossing closed-unit cone
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, a characteristic-$p$ field $k$, and a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$. Let $B=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ be affine etale with reduced strict normal crossings boundary $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ whose branches are precisely $V(t_d)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ be affine pro-etale [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Partition $\{1,\ldots,r\}=I_o\sqcup I_i$, $I_i\ne\varnothing$, let $a:V=U[1/\prod_{d\in I_o}t_d]\hookrightarrow U$, let $W=V[1/\prod_{d\in I_i}t_d]$, and let $h:Z=(V\setminus W)_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow V$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $s:S=V_U(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\hookrightarrow U$. For nonempty $J\subseteq I_i$ put $U_J=V_U(t_j:j\in J)$ and $V_J=U_J\times_U V$, with closed inclusions $g_J:U_J\hookrightarrow U$ and $d_J:V_J\hookrightarrow V$.
Let $C$ be a commutative condensed ring, use $C_X=p_X^*C$ and internal modules on small pro-etale sites, and take ordinary derived pushforwards and exact inverse images [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_V})$ and $H\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_U})$. Suppose supplied isomorphisms
$$\lambda:Ra_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}H,\qquad\mu_J:Ra_*d_{J,*}d_J^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{J,*}g_J^*H$$
intertwine the closed units $K\to d_{J,*}d_J^*K$ and $H\to g_{J,*}g_J^*H$ via $\lambda$, and intertwine all successive restriction maps for $J\subseteq J'$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Put $A_S=s^*H$ and
$$D=\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(s^*Ra_*K\xrightarrow{s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K})}s^*Ra_*h_*h^*K\bigr).$$
The coordinate schemes $V_{\{d\}}$ are reduced, factor through $Z$, cover its underlying closed set, and their scheme-theoretic intersections are $V_J$. All complementary open immersions needed for this finite closed cover are quasi-compact morphisms. The object $D$ admits a finite decreasing filtration by a tower of distinguished triangles in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_S})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. With $m=|I_i|$, its graded object in horizontal degree $-1$ is $A_S[1]$, and in horizontal degree $a$, $0\le a\le m-1$, is
$$\bigoplus_{|J|=a+1} A_S[-a].$$
All other graded objects are zero. Under these identifications, the first-page row in vertical degree $b$ of the cohomological exact-couple spectral sequence of this tower [def-sp-spectral-sequence] is
$$\mathcal H^b(A_S)\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{|J|=1}\mathcal H^b(A_S)\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{|J|=m}\mathcal H^b(A_S),$$
with the augmentation object in horizontal degree $-1$, diagonal augmentation, and signed alternating identity face maps. The filtration comes from a finite alternating closed-restriction resolution with its actual unit augmentation; the identification is in the derived category and does not assert strict chain-level constancy. These data are natural in maps of the supplied diagrams and in pullbacks for which $\lambda,\mu_J$ and the closed-restriction comparisons are identified, including profinite-parametrized diagrams. The case $I_o=\varnothing$ and empty $S$ are included. No vanishing of $D$ or invertibility of its defining map is asserted.

proof.text: Write $B_d=V_B(t_d)$. By the branch hypothesis these are the integral regular components in [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], hence are reduced and locally Noetherian. As an object of the pro-etale site of $B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $U\to B$ is weakly etale, hence flat. Its base change to any field-valued point is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. For every field-valued point of $B$, its affine fibre is weakly etale over a field and is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field]. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback] to $U\to B$ and the reduced locally Noetherian scheme $B_d$: $U_{\{d\}}$ is reduced. Its open subscheme $V_{\{d\}}$ is reduced because its local rings are unchanged. No Noetherian hypothesis on $U$ is used.

source.place: Tag 092Q, lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field, and following lemma-class-weakly-etale-over-field; reduced pullback as in the cited Mathlib leaf; etale.tex Tag 0BIA, lemma-strict-normal-crossings

proof.text: Put $R_o=R[1/\prod_{d\in I_o}t_d]$. In this affine ring, $Z$ has ideal $\sqrt{(\prod_{d\in I_i}t_d)}$. By step 1 each $(t_d)\subset R_o$ is radical; it contains that radical product ideal, so the quotient map to $R_o/(t_d)$ factors through the quotient defining $Z$. This proves scheme-theoretic factorization, not just containment of images. A prime contains $\prod_{d\in I_i}t_d$ exactly when it contains some $t_d$, so the supports cover $Z$. The intersection indexed by $J$ has quotient ring $R_o/(t_j:j\in J)$: a ring map factors through all the quotients precisely when it kills their sum. Localization commutes with this quotient by the same universal property, giving exactly $V_J$. These arguments include zero quotient rings and empty intersections.

source.place: Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme; affine radical-ideal and quotient universal-property calculation

proof.text: The complement of any coordinate intersection $V_J$ is $\bigcup_{j\in J}D(t_j)$; complements of unions of coordinate branches are principal opens $D(\prod t_j)$. Every such open immersion is quasi-compact as a morphism: on an arbitrary affine open of its target, restrict the finitely many defining functions; its inverse image is a finite union of principal spectra, each quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. A cover of a finite union has a finite subcover by choosing one for each member. The same argument works on every closed coordinate intersection and on $Z$, with the restricted functions. This verifies the complementary-open hypotheses of the closed-cover lemma and of the closed counits used below, including those for $g_J:U_J\hookrightarrow U$.

source.place: Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine; quasi-compactness of finite unions of principal opens, checked on arbitrary affine target opens

proof.text: Use the increasing order inherited by $I_i$. The coefficient ring on a closed face is the inverse image of $C_V$: composition of inverse images applied to $p_V^*C$ gives $p_{V_J}^*C$. By [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact] this transport is exact for arbitrary $C$, with no restriction to finite coefficients. For a bounded-below representative $L$ of $K$, apply [lem-sfb-finite-closed-cover-resolution] to $X=V$, $i=h$, and the cover $V_{\{d\}}$. Steps 1–3 verify all its geometric assumptions. Denote its total by $E(L)$, with columns $E^a(L)=\bigoplus_{|J|=a+1}d_{J,*}d_J^*L$ for $0\le a<m$. It supplies a quasi-isomorphism $h_*h^*L\to E(L)$, and its composite with the actual unit on $L$ is the diagonal singleton unit $u:L\to E(L)$. All differentials are the actual nested-face units with alternating signs.

source.place: Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open, via the existing finite-closed-cover-resolution node with its actual augmentation

proof.text: Form $M=\operatorname{Cone}(u:L\to E(L))$. Regard $L$ as column $-1$, with vertical differential $-d_L$, and $E^a(L)$ as column $a$, with vertical differential $(-1)^a d_L$. The total differential is the alternating face differential plus these vertical differentials. This is the cone matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_E&u\\0&-d_L\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F^pM$ retain exactly the columns $a\ge p$. The horizontal differential raises $a$ and the vertical differential preserves it, so these are subcomplexes; $F^{-1}M=M$ and $F^mM=0$. Projection to column $p$ gives a degreewise split exact sequence $0\to F^{p+1}M\to F^pM\to E^p(L)[-p]\to0$, where $E^{-1}(L)=L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-derived-triangle] each sequence gives its distinguished triangle. The graded pieces are $K[1]$ at $-1$ and $\bigoplus_{|J|=p+1}d_{J,*}d_J^*K[-p]$ at $p\ge0$.

source.place: Tags 014I and 014Q, split sequences and cone triangles; homology.tex Tag 012X, section-double-complex, horizontal filtration

proof.text: The categories of sheaves of $C_X$-modules on the chosen small sites are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], so have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Apply the general abelian-category clause of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts] to $a_*$ and then the exact termwise filtered lift of $s^*$. This yields a bounded-below finite filtered derived object $N$ with underlying object $s^*Ra_*M$. Its filtration-step triangles and their graded comparisons are those of [lem-trf-filtered-truncation-triangle]. In particular its grades are $s^*Ra_*K[1]$ and $\bigoplus_{|J|=a+1}s^*Ra_*d_{J,*}d_J^*K[-a]$: additive functors preserve finite biproducts. The quasi-isomorphism and augmentation of step 4 identify its underlying object with $D$, since this filtered lift is exact and its forgetful functor is the ordinary derived functor. Transport this specified tower along that identification; no cone is chosen functorially on arbitrary triangles.

source.place: Tag 015Q, lemma-filtered-localization-functor; Tag 05U2, equation-definition-filtered-derived-functor, and equations equation-commute-gr / equation-commute-forget

proof.text: For every nonempty $J$, let $q_J:S\to U_J$ be the unique closed factorization of $s$, which exists because each $t_j$ vanishes on $S$. Write $\eta_J$ for the actual unit of $g_J^*\dashv g_{J,*}$ and $\varepsilon_J$ for its counit. The canonical composition identifications give an isomorphism $\tau_J:s^*g_{J,*}g_J^*H=q_J^*g_J^*g_{J,*}g_J^*H\to q_J^*g_J^*H=s^*H$ obtained by $q_J^*\varepsilon_{J,g_J^*H}$. It is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-closed-counit], exactness of closed direct images and inverse images, and their derived normalization [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization]. The adjunction triangle identity says $\tau_J\,s^*\eta_J=1$. Thus $\rho_J=s^*\eta_J$ is exactly $\tau_J^{-1}$, not an unspecified isomorphism. Compose the graded comparisons of step 6 with $s^*\lambda$ and $\tau_Js^*\mu_J$. This gives the asserted grades $A_S[1]$ and $\bigoplus_{|J|=a+1}A_S[-a]$.

source.place: Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion; Tag 09BM, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact; actual counit and adjunction triangle identity

proof.text: For $J\subset J'$ write $g_{J'}=g_Je$ and $r_{JJ'}:g_{J,*}g_J^*H\to g_{J',*}g_{J'}^*H$ for the successive actual restriction. The composite-unit formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], with its derived identification from [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization], gives $r_{JJ'}\eta_J=\eta_{J'}$. After pulling back to $S$, the invertible maps $\rho_J$ of step 7 therefore satisfy $(s^*r_{JJ'})\rho_J=\rho_{J'}$. Hence $\tau_{J'}(s^*r_{JJ'})\tau_J^{-1}=1_{A_S}$. The assumed compatibility of $\lambda,\mu_J$ with all these maps now identifies every unsigned face map with the identity and the augmentation with the diagonal. The signs remain precisely $(-1)^\nu$ for deletion of the $\nu$-th entry of the ordered target subset; addition and inverse image preserve those signs.

source.place: Canonical composition of derived adjunctions, as in the cited normalization node; homology.tex Tag 012X, ordered alternating total differential

proof.text: Apply [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] to a finite filtered representative of $N$. Its first page is $\mathcal H^{a+b}(\operatorname{gr}^aN)$, and $d_1$ is the connecting map for the two-column filtration quotient. This is also the first page of the exact couple of the tower: there $E_1^{a,b}=\mathcal H^{a+b}(\operatorname{gr}^aN)$ and $d_1$ is the composite of $\mathcal H^{a+b}(\operatorname{gr}^aN)\to\mathcal H^{a+b+1}(F^{a+1}N)$ with $\mathcal H^{a+b+1}(F^{a+1}N)\to\mathcal H^{a+b+1}(\operatorname{gr}^{a+1}N)$, and the map of short exact sequences from $0\to F^{a+1}\to F^a\to\operatorname{gr}^a\to0$ to $0\to F^{a+1}/F^{a+2}\to F^a/F^{a+2}\to\operatorname{gr}^a\to0$ identifies this composite with the two-column connecting map by naturality of connecting maps. Before applying $s^*Ra_*$, that quotient is split in each cochain degree. Its connecting map is the off-diagonal entry $\pi d\iota$ by [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-derived-triangle], namely the horizontal restriction differential from column $a$ to column $a+1$ (including $u$ when $a=-1$). The exact filtered functor of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts] carries this triangle and connecting map to those for $N$, so this computation remains valid after derivation without strict chain-level identifications of the image columns. Using steps 7–8 gives $E_1^{a,b}=\bigoplus_{|J|=a+1}\mathcal H^b(A_S)$ for $a\ge0$, and $E_1^{-1,b}=\mathcal H^{b-1}(A_S[1])=\mathcal H^b(A_S)$, with exactly the diagonal augmentation and signed identity faces asserted.

source.place: Tag 012X, section-double-complex, lemma-ss-double-complex parts (1) and (3); derived.tex Tags 014I, 014Q and 05U2 for the transported connecting map

proof.text: The resolution and its augmentation are natural for the diagram maps and identified pullbacks specified in [lem-sfb-finite-closed-cover-resolution]. Taking the explicit augmented total, its column truncations and degreewise projections commutes with these maps. The filtered lifts and truncation comparisons used in steps 6 and 9 are natural by their cited statements. Finally $q_J^*\varepsilon_J$ is natural, so steps 7–8 identify the entire maps of graded diagrams, not only individual objects. Therefore the resulting filtered data and first-page identifications have the stated naturality. This applies equally to an entire profinite-parametrized diagram whenever its supplied comparisons are identified; no pointwise detection is used. If $I_o=\varnothing$, the outer product is $1$ and $a$ is the identity. For $m=1$ the row is the identity $\mathcal H^b(A_S)\to\mathcal H^b(A_S)$. If $S$ is empty all restrictions are zero. We have constructed the filtration and its first page only; no vanishing argument is needed.
